page_title: Writing Your Own Toy Compiler Using Flex, Bison and LLVM

sources.entry: C++: _Writing Your Own Toy Compiler Using Flex_

summary.title: Writing Your Own Toy Compiler Using Flex, Bison and LLVM
summary.one_liner: You learn how to build a small toy language compiler in C++ by lexing with Flex, parsing into an AST with Bison, and generating LLVM code that runs via JIT.
keywords: how to write a compiler step by step
takeaways: Lexical analysis with Flex splits source text into tokens such as identifiers, numbers, operators and braces.
Bison grammar rules with semantic actions build an AST whose node classes are defined in node.h.
Each AST node implements codeGen() which walks the tree and emits LLVM IR, which is then run with LLVM's JIT.
The toy language supports functions, variables, assignment and basic math on int and double types; some features such as return and comparisons are left as exercises.
summary.summary: The article is a step-by-step tutorial for building a minimal C-like toy language compiler. It walks through three stages: a Flex lexer (tokens.l), a Bison parser that builds an AST (parser.y and node.h), and LLVM-based code generation (codegen.h and codegen.cpp) executed with the LLVM JIT. It includes full listings of the source files and build commands, and notes that parts of the language are left unimplemented for the reader. The page is an update for LLVM 2.6 and uses older LLVM APIs, and the author warns that LLVM documentation is sparse and out of date.
